fields.questionText: (i) What is a solenoid? Draw a diagram showing the magnetic field pattern due to a current-carrying solenoid (inside and outside). (ii) Name any two factors on which the magnitude of the magnetic field due to a current-carrying solenoid depends. (iii) A current-carrying solenoid is stretched and converted into a straight wire carrying current. Draw a diagram showing the magnetic field pattern around it and mark the direction of the magnetic field.
fields.answer: (i) A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder; inside it the field lines are parallel straight lines (uniform field), outside they resemble those of a bar magnet. (ii) The current through the solenoid and the number of turns of the coil. (iii) Concentric circles around the wire, direction given by the right-hand thumb rule.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (i) Solenoid: a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.

[1 mark] Diagram: inside the solenoid the field lines are parallel straight lines (uniform field); outside they run from one end (N) to the other (S), like the field of a bar magnet, with directions of current and field marked.
[1 mark] (ii) Factors: (1) magnitude of the current flowing through the solenoid; (2) number of turns of the coil (per unit length).
[1 mark] (iii) Diagram: for a straight current-carrying wire, the field lines are concentric circles centred on the wire, in planes perpendicular to it.

[1 mark] Direction marked using the right-hand thumb rule (thumb along current, curled fingers give field direction). Marks are awarded if a different current direction is shown with the correct corresponding field direction.
fields.finalAnswer: (i) Closely wound cylindrical coil of insulated wire; uniform parallel field inside, bar-magnet-like field outside. (ii) Current and number of turns. (iii) Concentric circles around the wire, direction by the right-hand thumb rule.

fields.questionText: A circular coil carries a current that flows anticlockwise when the coil is viewed from its front face. Draw the magnetic field lines for this coil. Decide which of its faces behaves as the North pole and which face as the South pole. Give reason to justify your answer.
fields.answer: The front face behaves as the North pole and the back face as the South pole, because the magnetic field lines emerge from the front face and enter the coil at the back face.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Field lines: concentric loops around each part of the wire, becoming nearly straight and parallel near the centre of the coil, emerging from the front face and entering at the back face.
[1 mark] Using the right-hand thumb rule (or the clock-face rule): current anticlockwise when viewed from a face means field lines come out of that face, so the front face is the North pole.
[1 mark] The back face (current appears clockwise from there) has field lines entering it, so it is the South pole.
fields.finalAnswer: Front face — North pole; back face — South pole (field lines emerge from the front face).
